what: Newmont is the world's largest gold miner, with operations across the Americas, Africa, Australia and Papua New Guinea. It also produces copper, silver, lead and zinc from the same mines.
customers: Refiners and bullion markets for gold; smelters and traders for copper and other metals.
money: production from mines in twelve countries
copper, silver, lead and zinc recovered alongside gold
moat: A portfolio of very large, long-life mines in mostly stable jurisdictions, and reserves of more than 100 million ounces that would take decades to replace.
risks: Profit depends on the gold price, which the company does not control
Mining cost inflation has eaten into margins across the industry
Operations in Papua New Guinea, Ghana and Argentina carry political risk
Integrating the Newcrest acquisition involved selling several mines
opportunities: A high gold price has lifted revenue about 21% and produced large free cash flow
Selling smaller mines concentrates the portfolio on the best assets
Copper output grows with gold mining and benefits from electrification demand
watch: All-in sustaining cost per ounce, which shows how much of a high gold price it keeps.
